business_problem: WWF Germany needed a faster, more reliable way to find ghost nets hidden in large volumes of archived sonar data because manual review was slow, costly, and too inconsistent to support large-scale recovery operations.
solution_summary: WWF Germany partnered with Accenture and Microsoft's AI for Good Lab to create GhostNetZero, an AI-powered platform that turns raw sonar scans into usable recovery targets for ghost-net removal teams. Sonar data from scientific surveys, seabed mapping, and navigation programs is uploaded into the platform instead of being left in archives. AI models scan the files, identify suspicious patterns that may indicate lost fishing gear, and flag candidate targets for marine experts to validate. Confirmed locations are then logged, mapped, and shared through a dashboard that expands as new data donors contribute files across countries. The system creates a shared knowledge base of underwater hazards while keeping participation simple through secure architecture and live dashboards. By combining sonar ingestion, AI detection, expert validation, and shared mapping, GhostNetZero shifts ghost-net recovery from manual footage review to a repeatable digital workflow that is easier to scale region by region.

data_flow: Research and survey organizations upload sonar scans to GhostNetZero, where AI models analyze files and flag likely ghost-net targets. Marine experts validate those hits, and confirmed targets are logged and mapped in the platform dashboard so recovery teams and new partners can act on the growing shared data set.
business_outcome: WWF Germany reduced the labor needed to inspect sonar data, improved detection accuracy, and created a scalable collaboration model that helps turn previously unused survey data into actionable recovery work for ghost-net removal.
